own_solution.law: With primary rms voltage U, the secondary peak is Vp = sqrt(2)*U/4. The load voltage is max(Vp*|sin(theta)| - 1.4 V, 0). Defining alpha = asin(1.4 V/Vp), its average is (2/pi)*(Vp*cos(alpha) - 1.4 V*(pi/2-alpha)). At U = 230 V this gives 50.3759 V.
assumptions: The average is over a complete cycle of the sinusoidal supply.
The stated ideal-transformer and constant-drop diode models apply.
The lamp's variable supply has no electrical connection specified to the rectifier circuit.
The resistive load and absence of energy storage make the measured voltage independent of earlier runs.

notes: All certified answers agree with the stated relations: increasing the primary rms voltage by 8, 14 and 21 V gives 52.1762, 53.5265 and 55.1019 V, respectively. Positive load resistances of 18, 47 and 82 ohms cancel between current and load voltage. The lamp changes and earlier-run changes have no path to the measured voltage.
